hero.caption:
Scope and content:  Original Caption: German Super U-boats interned in French port. German super-submarines, including the Deutschland II, a sister ship to be notorious undersea craft which made the cross Atlantic trip to American, which are now interned in the French port at Cherbourg.
Photographer: Underwood and Underwood

images.caption: Torpilleur No. 65 (French torpedo boat, 1884-1903). Photographed at Cherbourg Dockyard in the summer of 1884; this ship ran her trials from this port during May to July 1884. The coast defense ship Fulminant (1877-1912), fitting out, appears in the far right; the armored cruiser Vauban (1882-1914) is just behind Fulminant, also fitting out at a slow pace. Naval History and Heritage Command.

171018-N-FP878-160

CHERBOURG, France (Oct. 18, 2017) Cmdr. Timothy Moore, commanding officer of the Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer, USS Donald Cook (DDG 75), exchanges gifts with Capt. Bertrand Hudault, French deputy commander for the North Sea and English Channel, during an office call in Cherbourg, France, Oct. 18, 2017.  Donald Cook, forward-deployed to Rota, Spain, is on its sixth patrol in the U.S. 6th Fleet area of operations in support of regional allies and partners, and U.S. national security interests in Europe. (U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Theron J. Godbold /Released)
